messages:
rachel: Heads-up: after the route-priority header change landed in canary, TS client batching started dropping second requests in a multi-request batch. Observed in canary-4.

jong: Ugh. Is this the header rename or the value format?

ivan: Repro steps: create 3 small generate calls in a single batch; the middleware attaches `x-rd-route-priority: \"p1\"` and batching layer collapses into a single RPC with only the first call.

lily: That sounds like a batch-key collision. We changed batch-key to include `route.priority` under the new header name but didn't account for arrays.

rachel: Minimal log: 
```
batch_keys: ["model:gpt-3.5|route.priority:p1","model:gpt-3.5|route.priority:p1","model:gpt-3.5|route.priority:p1"]
sent payloads: [1, -, -]
```

jong: So the batcher treats identical keys as idempotent payloads and keeps only one. Old behavior used `route_meta.route_id` so collisions were rare.

ivan: Root cause: TS SDK's canonicalizer flattens priority into a string and loses request-scoped id. Fix: include request nonce in batch key or use composite key with array index.

lily: Can we patch server to be tolerant? Short-term: server-side batcher can fall back to per-request routing when same key seen multiple payloads. That's heavier but safe for canary.

qa-bot: Created ticket DEVX-1401: "TS batching collision with new route-priority header". Tests failing: batch-sanity.js x3. Tagging CI.

ci-bot: CI: canary pipeline failing for ts-client canary-4: 2/12 tests failed. See https://ci.redwood.ai/flow/1234.

jong: Plan: 1) Hotfix TS SDK to append short nonce to batch key (minor patch) and ship canary client. 2) Server-side fallback while SDKs roll. 3) Add telemetry tile showing `batch.collapse_rate` by route header and by client version.

ivan: I'll open PR for TS: add `batchKeyNonce: nanoid(6)` appended to the key when `route.priority` exists. Will keep opt-in behind flag but default on canary.

lily: Server-side fallback: will mark batch as "sensitive" if identical route-priority and payload counts >1, then split into per-request sub-batches. Deploy to canary tomorrow.

rachel: Telemetry: we need a fast way to detect regressions in production. Add a console dashboard: axes = batch size vs collapse_rate, filter by `client.semver` and `route.priority`. Set anomaly alert if collapse_rate > 5% and client.semver >= 2.1.0.

qa-bot: I can add e2e that simulates 1000 multi-request batches across priorities and asserts collapse_rate < 0.1%. Adding to canary smoke.

ci-bot: Patch build for ts-sdk: https://github.com/redwood/ts-sdk/pull/2145 | status: draft.

ivan: Draft PR ready for review, includes changelog entry and migration note: "TS batching keys now include nonce when route-priority present to avoid collisions; no server changes required."

jong: We should still announce to integrators because other clients may be affected. Also verify Py/Go behavior—do they already include nonce?

lily: Py/Go include `request_id` in batch key by default so they're fine. Only TS omitted it for perf reasons.

rachel: OK. Timeline: TS hotfix canary today, server fallback in canary tomorrow, telemetry tile up in 48h, broader SDK patch release next week with migration note.

ivan: I'll land the canary PR after two approvals.

rachel: Thx. After relicensing, post a short note in #platform-integrations and add a console banner for 7 days noting the transient canary issue.

jong: +1. Also file a postmortem template if this leaks to prod. Keep messages short.

qa-bot: Adding synthetic test to periodic suite to prevent regressions.

rachel: Great team. Keep me posted.
